assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), receptor biology) led to incretin therapies that have transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. This is an unusually clear arc from basic hormone physiology to a medicine with large, durable clinical impact, and fits the physiology-to-medicine tradition well.
assessment.attribution: Holst (isolation and physiology of the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, receptor and therapeutic proof of concept) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry, identification of the active form) form a plausible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's drug-development role is important but is industrial and is left out to respect the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Cardiometabolic outcome trials, weight-loss data and widespread clinical use give strong independent confirmation over more than a decade; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener and others for the active peptide form is contested, and Habener is not on the credited list.
Whether the committee prefers a discovery-level or a drug-development-level framing is unresolved.
I am relying on my own recollection of the literature rather than verifying details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new mode of intracellular signaling from the ER to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory biology, metabolism, neurodegeneration, cancer and aging. The discovery is conceptually original, clean and widely generalizable.
assessment.attribution: Walter (Ire1 as the stress sensor, the UPR concept and its mechanism) and Mori (UPR element and HAC1/XBP1 transcription factor pathway) are the standard pairing, with a tidy two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation across yeast, metazoans and disease models; the core mechanism is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation (for example ISRIB-type or IRE1/PERK modulators) is still maturing, so medical impact is more indirect.
Contributions of others, such as Kohno and Sidrauski/Ron on PERK and ATF6, may complicate a narrow credit story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells directed against tumor antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, creating a new class of living drug. The clinical impact in leukemia and lymphoma is substantial and the concept is original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early chimeric receptor and costimulation design), June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cell trials) cover scientific and clinical contributions. Eshhar and others who preceded them are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and multi-year follow-up are strong; durability, toxicity, solid-tumor limits and access are still evolving, so the field is mature for hematologic disease but not for cancer generally.
uncertainties: Priority for the original chimeric receptor concept (Eshhar and colleagues) is not captured by the supplied credited names.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being characterized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified a neuropeptide system that is central to sleep-wake stability and the cause of narcolepsy type 1. The finding connected a gene, a receptor mutation in dogs, loss of neurons in patients, and now orexin receptor antagonists and agonists in the clinic.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexin and its receptors and the knockout phenotype; Mignot identified the canine narcolepsy gene (Hcrtr2) and the human orexin deficiency. De Lecea and Kilduff reported hypocretin independently, which creates a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Strongly replicated and now clinically validated by suvorexant-type drugs and ongoing orexin agonist trials; timing is good.
uncertainties: Priority between orexin and hypocretin groups is a classic dual-discovery dispute and the three-person limit forces exclusion of de Lecea and Kilduff.
Role of Mignot versus others in the human pathogenesis may be weighted differently by different members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type specific control of activity with millisecond precision, and has reshaped circuit analysis across systems. As a methodological invention its impact on discovery is very large.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) established channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth (and Boyden) established its use in neurons and in vivo. Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck have strong claims, so any three-person subset leaves out defensible contributors.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for two decades and confirmed independently; clinical translation (retinal optogenetics) is only beginning.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit across six credited names is genuinely contested.
The prize's emphasis on tools versus discoveries about disease could lower its standing relative to therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, and that blocking it helps patients, launched anti-cytokine therapy across several inflammatory diseases. The translational chain from mechanism to medicine is clean and broadly impactful.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the clinical and scientific proof-of-concept leads and form a natural pair. Contributions from the discoverers of TNF and the antibody developers (for example Vilcek, Cerami) are not in the supplied credited names.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of widespread use in several diseases with clear independent confirmation; recognition is timely if not early.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as a therapy-application of earlier cytokine biology that was itself not recognized.
Biosimilar-era saturation does not affect worthiness but may affect perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 defined the survival arm of apoptosis control, explained how oncogene-driven lymphoma escapes cell death, and led to BH3-mimetic drugs such as venetoclax. It combines conceptual originality with a successful targeted drug.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the molecular analysis of Bcl-2 and its family; Vaux and Strasser contributed key functional and mechanistic work. Others outside the list (Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer, Reed) matter for the t(14;18) and mechanism story. A two-person configuration is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Well-established and clinically validated in CLL and AML; apoptosis itself is already recognized, so incremental recognition for BCL-2 is plausible but may feel secondary.
uncertainties: Apoptosis was recognized in 2002, so some members may regard BCL-2 as an extension rather than a new discovery.
Credit in the cloning of the translocation partner is shared with groups not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR defined a central nutrient- and growth-factor-sensing kinase that couples metabolism to cell growth, with relevance to cancer, diabetes, immunosuppression and aging. The discovery is conceptually foundational and widely cited.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and showed it is the target of rapamycin; Schreiber's chemical-genetic work with FKBP12-rapamycin and mTOR contributed to target identification, while Sabatini's mammalian pathway work is substantial but he is left out here. Heitman, Sabatini and Brown/Sabers have competing claims.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across species and pathways, with rapalogs in clinical use; some mechanistic questions about mTORC1 and mTORC2 regulation remain active.
uncertainties: Competing claims over who identified mammalian mTOR could complicate attribution.
Therapeutic benefit of rapalogs is real but modest, so the case rests mainly on basic-science importance.
